subject: Request: log hold and retention amendment — DPA/subprocessor questions
messages:
From: Anika Rao <anika.rao@medisol.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>; kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: security@medisol.com
Date: Fri, 14 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: extended log retention & emergency snapshot hold - DPA impact

Hi Priyom / Kimberly,

We're preparing for an upcoming regulatory audit and we need Redwood's help with two items that intersect with the DPA:

1) A temporary snapshot hold for a defined set of application logs (auth & transaction traces) for 12 months from capture date — we understand your default is shorter.
2) A pause on routine backup purge for the affected buckets while the hold is in place.

The auditor has requested evidence that logs were retained and immutable for the requested window. Please confirm: which subprocessors touch the backup pipeline (including cross-border transfer vendors), whether KMS keys are customer or Redwood-managed for these snapshots, and an estimate for how long you can operationally hold snapshot data without impacting system SLOs.

I've attached an AuditRequest summary and a high-level list of sample IDs. Can you confirm next steps and who on your side will own a DPA amendment or retention carve-out?

Thanks,
Anika Rao
Head of Security & Compliance
MediSol Health

Attachments: AuditRequest_20251114.pdf (summary of auditor requests, sample log IDs)

From: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>

Subject: Re: Request: extended log retention & emergency snapshot hold - DPA impact

Anika — thanks for the clear ask and the attachment. We're able to support a temporary exception but need to align legal, security, and engineering on scope and timeline.

Immediate answers to two of your questions:
- Subprocessors that touch our backup pipeline (shortlist): StorageWave (long‑term snapshots), CloudCopy Inc. (cross‑region replication). I'll confirm the full list after procurement lookup.
- KMS: by default Redwood manages the service KMS for system-level snapshots; we can support customer-managed keys in Private deployments only.

Next steps from our side:
1) I'll loop in Legal/Compliance to scope a DPA amendment (kimberly).
2) Engineering to confirm the operational impact and propose a snapshot hold procedure (cc: laura, marcus).
3) We will propose a timeboxed approach rather than a blanket 12‑month retention; suggest interim 180 days while legal agrees the DPA addendum.

Can you confirm which exact datasets (bucket prefixes / log prefixes) you need held and whether you require immutability (WORM) or just nondestructive retention?

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Lead, Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Quick engineering readout:

Scope & feasibility:
- We can tag snapshot objects with a "hold:medisol-audit-2025" metadata flag and have lifecycle policies skip objects with that flag.
- Default retention for logs in our hosted environment is 90 days (cold snapshots 30 days). Holding snapshots for 12 months is technically feasible but will materially increase storage spend; 180 days is a reasonable compromise for evidence collection.

Subprocessors and transfer notes:
- Backup flow: app logs --> internal ingestion (Redwood S3/us-west-2) --> StorageWave for long-term archival (s3://storagewave-archive, US region) --> CloudCopy Inc. for cross-region replication (us-east-1).
- StorageWave is a subprocessor; we currently have a Data Processing Addendum listing them. They use a US-based storage provider but sometimes replicate for resilience. No EU copies for this account unless directed.

Operational steps for a hold:
1) Customer identifies exact prefixes and confirms immutability requirement.
2) Run a hold job: tag objects and create a snapshot manifest.
3) Suspend lifecycle rules on matching prefixes for the agreed window.
4) Generate a signed certificate of preservation and provide auditor access to audit logs (read-only).

Costs & timeline:
- Estimated incremental storage: ~$0.06/GB/month for archival tier; rough estimate for Medisol sample set is $2.4K/month for 180 days (TBC).
- Engineering can run a pilot in 48 hours once we have prefixes and a signed amendment.

I'll assemble the exact object listing and a command runbook.

— Marcus Lin
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.inference.com>

Date: Sun, 16 Nov 2025 11:15:00 -0800
Subject: Compliance stance & gating items for retention carve-out

Team — reviewing the ask from a security/compliance lens. Proposed constraints:

1) Approve timeboxed exception: 180 days maximum for the specific log prefixes Anika will provide. 12 months is a bigger legal lift and requires an exception request to the InfoSec Review Board and an elevated SLA credit.
2) Require DocuSign DPA amendment that includes: dataset identifiers, retention window, subprocessor list (StorageWave, CloudCopy Inc.), and a statement on cross-border replication.
3) For hosted customers: ensure we provide a signed preservation certificate and read-only access to audit logs.
4) KMS & access: if Redwood-managed keys are used, restrict key rotation and provide key-access audit trail. If Medisol requires customer-managed keys, escalate to Private deployment lane.

I'll approve the 180-day carve-out once the DocuSign amendment is in place and Marcus confirms the hold job runbook. We should also capture estimated incremental cost and provide Medisol an APR (approval + cost estimate) before DocuSign.

— Soojin Lee
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Anika — thanks for your patience. Summary and proposed next steps below.

What we can do now (agreed):
- Redwood will implement a timeboxed snapshot hold for the specified log prefixes. Security has approved a 180-day maximum window pending a signed DPA amendment.
- Subprocessors in-scope: StorageWave (long-term archival), CloudCopy Inc. (cross-region replication). No EU copies will be created for this account unless explicitly requested in the amendment.
- KMS: Hosted accounts will use Redwood-managed keys with restricted rotation for the hold window; Private deployments can use customer-managed keys.
- Operational pilot: engineering can run a hold pilot within 48 hours after we receive the full list of prefixes and a signed amendment.

Required from MediSol:
1) Exact bucket / prefix list (CSV or manifest).
2) Confirmation whether immutability (WORM) is required or a nondestructive hold suffices.
3) Signed DocuSign amendment (draft attached) — link: https://www.docusign.com/sign/ABCDEF-20251116

Estimated costs (preview): ~$2.4K/month for the sample scope for 180 days (final quote after manifest).

I've attached the draft amendment and the auditor request you sent. Once you sign, Kimberly will countersign and we will queue engineering for the pilot. We will also provide a preservation certificate and read-only auditor access once the hold is in place.

Next actions (owner):
- Medisol: send manifest + decide WORM vs hold (Anika) — due EOD Tue 18 Nov 2025.
- Redwood Legal: finalize & send DocuSign (Kimberly) — in progress.
- Engineering: build hold job & pilot (Marcus) — blocked until DocuSign and manifest.

Best,
